statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-92707 (GHSA-qhrr-8q5h-9q3h) is a denial of service in MessagePack for C#: MessagePackReader.ReadArrayHeader and ReadMapHeader only check that the declared element count does not exceed the unread bytes, so nested headers can reuse the same trailing bytes, and a consumer that allocates from the declared count before reading the elements (PrimitiveObjectFormatter, used when deserializing into System.Object) can be made to allocate about 3,800 times the payload size before the depth limit rejects it. The fix, in MessagePack-CSharp 2.5.303, replaces that check with ReserveMinimumChildBytes, which tracks the bytes already committed to enclosing containers (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qhrr-8q5h-9q3h; commit 7fd78bbf on the v2.x branch, https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/commit/7fd78bbf3476e03beae8b0f7a521125525a8a64a, merged to master as 95b63fca). Microsoft's advisory lists the affected packages as Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Protocols.MessagePack (10.0.0 through 10.0.12 affected, 10.0.13 fixed), MessagePack, MessagePack.Annotations and MessagePackAnalyzer; ASP.NET Core v10.0.13 fixed it by moving its MessagePack package reference from 2.5.302 to 2.5.303, and no file under src/Components changed for it (https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/473, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release. Scanned every file of all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, recursing into the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: no file name contains MessagePack in any letter case, so no build ships MessagePack.dll, MessagePack.Annotations.dll, the analyzer, or the Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Protocols.MessagePack assembly or nupkg (the same search finds Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Protocols.Json.dll in every build). A byte search of every file in the x86_64 dotnet10-runtime, aspnetcore10-runtime, dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap and dotnet10-runtime-artifacts packages of 10.0.2-r0 and 10.0.15-r0 found PrimitiveObjectFormatter in no file (the same search finds it in MessagePack.dll 2.5.301 and 2.5.303 from NuGet) and MessagePack code only in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.dll (the other matches are license notices, XML documentation, symbol files and MSBuild's unrelated LogMessagePacket type). Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.dll compiles in MessagePack-CSharp's MessagePackReader and MessagePackWriter source for the Blazor Server hub protocol (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v10.0.13/src/Components/Server/src/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.csproj), and that copy is unfixed in most builds: the assembly from the aspnetcore10-runtime package of every published build on both architectures (24 files, package checksums verified against the index) contains ReadArrayHeader and ThrowInsufficientBufferUnless, but in 10.0.2-r0 through 10.0.14-r0 contains neither ReserveMinimumChildBytes nor minimumRemainingChildBytes. Decompiling the x86_64 copies of 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0 and 10.0.14-r0 shows ReadArrayHeader as TryReadArrayHeader followed by ThrowInsufficientBufferUnless(reader.Remaining >= count), the pre-fix routine, with the sequence reader, the cancellation token and Depth as the reader's only fields. From 10.0.15-r0 the copy carries the fix (ReadArrayHeader calls ReserveMinimumChildBytes), because ASP.NET Core's MessagePack-CSharp submodule moved to a commit that includes 7fd78bbf (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69541) (the .NET 10 source as built, https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/v10.0.15/src/aspnetcore/src/submodules/MessagePack-CSharp/src/MessagePack.UnityClient/Assets/Scripts/MessagePack/MessagePackReader.cs, carries it at v10.0.15 and not at v10.0.13); that was a routine dependency update, not part of the CVE fix, and Microsoft does not list the ASP.NET Core shared framework as affected. The unfixed check cannot be exploited through this assembly. The amplification needs a caller that allocates from the declared element count before reading the elements and then descends into nested containers, and there is none: the decompiled assembly's only users of MessagePackReader are the shared MessagePackHubProtocolWorker and BlazorPackHubProtocolWorker (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v10.0.13/src/SignalR/common/Protocols.MessagePack/src/Protocol/MessagePackHubProtocolWorker.cs, https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v10.0.13/src/Components/Server/src/BlazorPack/BlazorPackHubProtocolWorker.cs). Their header reads are: the message array header, whose count is only compared with constants; the headers map, read into a Dictionary that grows as each key and value string is actually read; the argument array, whose count must equal the hub method's parameter count before new object[count] is allocated; the stream-id array, read into a List as each string is actually read; and Skip (also behind ReadRaw) for a completion result with no known return type, which is iterative, uses TryReadArrayHeader and TryReadMapHeader, and allocates nothing. Arguments are deserialized only as string, bool, int, long, float, byte[] or JsonElement (the last two from bytes that must be present in the message); any other MessagePack type in an argument position throws, so nothing in this assembly deserializes into System.Object or recurses into nested arrays or maps, and the Blazor hub's methods take only string, bool, int, long and byte[] parameters (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v10.0.13/src/Components/Server/src/ComponentHub.cs). An application that adds the SignalR MessagePack hub protocol brings Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Protocols.MessagePack and MessagePack.dll from NuGet itself; neither is part of this package.
